quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Electronics engineers research, design, develop or test electronic components and systems, and design electronic circuits and components for fields such as telecommunications.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Electronics Engineers, Except Computer) include Integrated Circuit Design Engineer (IC Design Engineer), Electronics Design Engineer, Radio Frequency Engineer and Product Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a chip design engineer does
paragraphs: Electronics engineers research, design, develop or test electronic components and systems, and design electronic circuits and components for fields such as telecommunications.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Electronics Engineers, Except Computer. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Design electronic components, products or systems for commercial, industrial or scientific use.
Use computer-assisted engineering and design software to do electronics engineering work.
Evaluate project work for effectiveness, technical adequacy and compatibility.
Discuss existing or planned electronics projects with engineers, customers and vendors.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
